verdicts.strongest_argument: The tape prices this twice, on the exact dates the information arrived, and has already round-tripped it. Confirmed closes: 15 Jul $3.65, 16 Jul $3.32 (-9% on the 21st-package LNG shipping ban threat), 22 Jul $3.69, 23 Jul $3.85 (+16% off the low on the Greek carve-out), 24 Jul $3.61 (-6.2%). Spot on 04 Sep is $3.66 - i.e. one cent above the pre-scare 15 July close. There is no residual carve-out premium left in the price to deflate, which is arithmetically fatal to the bearish inference regardless of whether the mechanism is right. On the mechanism itself: the third-country-deliveries-only limitation, the pre-24-Feb-2022 contract condition and the annual Council review were published in mainstream EU-policy press on 23 July 2026 - the very day of the rally peak - and in Steptoe/White & Case client alerts the same week; the stock then gave back 6.2% the next session. The 1 Jan 2027 EU restriction on the Yenisei River and Lena River Yamal charters is disclosed by the company itself in the 29 May 2026 Q1 6-K and the 8 Apr 2026 20-F, so the exposure is not news to anyone reading the issuer. Two factual notes. First, the finding's vessel-identity check is CORRECT and I verified it independently: the listed partnership's six hulls are Clean Energy, Ob River, Amur River, Arctic Aurora, Yenisei River and Lena River; Clean Planet and Clean Ocean sit under Dynagas Holding Ltd. and Clean Vision and Clean Horizon under Dynagas Equity Holding Ltd., i.e. the sponsor side, and urgewald's 18 Aug 2026 release does conflate them under 'Dynagas'. That is the highest-value unpublished element here and it is right. Second, the inference drawn from it is weak and arguably sign-reversed: the Article 3s-style derogation operates at the level of the EU (Greek) *operator* under pre-2022 contracts, not at the level of named hulls, so Dynagas Ltd's managed fleet - which includes DLNG's two Yamal ships - is inside it for third-country deliveries; and if only 2 of 6 listed hulls carry Yamal cargo against '5 of 14 Dynagas-linked Arc7' in the NGO framing, the honest read is that the NYSE entity carries *less* of the headline risk than the press release implies, which is a bull point, not a bear point. Third, the finding's renewal description is slightly wrong in the unhelpful direction: the derogation renews automatically for successive one-year periods unless the Council decides otherwise, it does not require an affirmative annual vote. Finally the Huelva datum is one voyage: Yamal Trade can and does redirect cargoes to third countries, and a legal August 2026 EU discharge says nothing about post-1-Jan-2027 routing. Channel is also poor - the 8 Sep release is a document plus a slide deck with no conference call, so there is no Q&A through which a sanctions re-framing can be forced into the price.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The Greek-won carve-out permits Russian LNG transport to third countries only, under pre-24-February-2022 contracts, with annual Council review - published on the day of the DLNG rally peak.
Law-firm alert setting out the 21st package derogation for LNG shipping services, its 25 July 2027 initial expiry, the annual renewal mechanism and the cap at the operator's 2025 volumes.

DLNG's own Q1 2026 release states that the Yenisei River and Lena River are on Yamal Trade charters to 2033 and 2034 and that new EU and UK sanctions effective 1 January 2027 will restrict them from transporting Russian LNG, potentially affecting charter continuance.

Names Clean Planet, Clean Vision, Clean Ocean and Clean Horizon, attributes 57 Yamal cargoes and EUR2.35bn of EU deliveries to 'Dynagas-linked' vessels, and does not distinguish the NYSE partnership from Dynagas Holding.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Verified daily closes: 3.65 (15 Jul) -> 3.32 (16 Jul) -> 3.69 (22 Jul) -> 3.85 (23 Jul) -> 3.61 (24 Jul); August range 3.71-3.90; spot 3.66 on 04 Sep. The baseline's -6.23% 'reaction' on 2026-07-23 is the 24 July give-back, and the 6-K it is attributed to is in fact only a Series A preferred distribution declaration (accession 0001317861-26-000035) - further confirmation the history block is not an earnings base rate. run_up_20d -2.66% and run_up_5d -4.94% show the name drifting back, not holding a sanctions premium. No option information exists (total OI 41, put/call OI 0.03), so the tape is the only instrument and it says the July round trip is complete.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that the derogation is drafted hull-by-hull rather than operator-by-operator, or that Yamal Trade has redelivered or suspended either the Yenisei River or the Lena River, would restore most of the edge.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The observation is real and I verified it from the same live page today (IMO 9323687 = CLEAN ENERGY, 2007-built, Marshall Islands; at anchor, South East Asia, 0.1 knots, draught 8.9 m against a 12.4 m laden draught, no destination, no ETA, last port Singapore Anch. 1 departed 5 August 06:58 UTC). I found no financial-media coverage of it, so the fact itself is close to unpublished. But two of the finding's three legs are old wire copy and the third is mis-specified. The Arctic Aurora seven-year Rio Grande charter commencing September-November 2026 and the Clean Energy two-year charter commencing March-May 2026 were both announced on 18 July 2023 and are restated in every 20-F since; 'a third of the fleet on hire to Rio Grande' has therefore been a published fact for three years. That Rio Grande's Brownsville trains are not producing is equally public - NextDecade's own 2026 business updates guide first gas H2 2026 and first LNG from Train 1 in H1 2027 - and it was never a surprise, because the 2023 charters were deliberately struck to start ahead of the plant. The mis-specification is the one that matters: these are time charters, so hire runs whether the charterer trades the ship or parks her, and a vessel idled at the charterer's direction is on-hire, not off-hire. The finding therefore does not demonstrate lost revenue; it demonstrates that Rio Grande LNG is paying for a steam-turbine carrier it has no cargo for, which is a counterparty-credit observation about NextDecade, not a DLNG revenue observation. And the timing kills the mechanism: the idling began 5 August 2026, which is Q3. The 8 September release covers the quarter ended 30 June, so this cannot appear in the reported numbers, and with no conference call there is no forum in which it can be raised. What genuinely does sit inside the Q2 window - roughly four weeks of Clean Energy off-hire between SEFE redelivery in early April and Rio Grande delivery at end-April - was already disclosed in the 29 May 2026 Q1 release. I also note a source conflict I cannot resolve: a MarineTraffic crawl surfaced in search shows the same IMO underway off the Indian coast at 13.2 knots, so the AIS aggregators disagree, and the reading is un-archivable and may have changed since it was taken.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Arctic Aurora fixed for about seven years commencing September-November 2026 and Clean Energy for about two years commencing March-May 2026, both to Rio Grande LNG, adding ~USD270m of backlog.
NextDecade guides first gas into Rio Grande in H2 2026 and first LNG from Train 1 in H1 2027, with Phase 1 tracking ahead of guaranteed substantial completion.
Discloses that Clean Energy was redelivered from SEFE in early April 2026 and delivered to Rio Grande at end-April 2026 at a higher daily rate, i.e. the Q2 off-hire gap is already company-disclosed.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move in the tape around 5 August - the stock traded 3.71-3.90 through August and drifted to 3.66, with realised 20d vol of only 24.5% annualised, i.e. no volatility signature of anyone discovering this. That cuts both ways: it is consistent with the fact being unknown, and equally consistent with it being irrelevant. There is no option market (total OI 41) to express a view either way, and 50,830 shares/day of 20-day average volume on a ~$135m cap means even a correct discovery cannot be expressed by the close on 8 September without a dedicated buyer or seller showing up.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A statement in the 8 September release or slide deck that Clean Energy is off-hire, or that the Rio Grande charter has been suspended, deferred or terminated, would make this material and largely unpriced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every factual element checks out - I confirmed one Form 3 filed 2026-03-18 and five filed 2026-03-30, all with event date 18 March 2026; the Prokopiou form reports 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units held indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd. with a 50.4% interest and the usual disclaimer; the FY2025 20-F was filed 2026-04-08 and 6-Ks have continued through 2026-08-13. So the finding is not wrong about anything. It is, however, split between a substantive part that is 95% priced and an anomaly with no demonstrated mechanism. The substance - Prokopiou/Dynagas Holding controlling 15,595,000 common units and the GP - has been in every 20-F and in the 2013 424B4 for a decade; there is nothing new in the number, and the Form 3s report no transaction, so they are not insider buying or selling and carry no directional content at all. The anomaly - an issuer exempt from Section 16 under Rule 3a12-3(b) filing Form 3s anyway - is genuinely obscure and I found zero media coverage of it. But the finding itself supplies the disconfirming evidence: five and a half months later there is no Form 4, no 10-Q, no transition to domestic-filer status and no Schedule 13E-3, and the issuer has kept filing on the foreign-private-issuer track. Absent any follow-through, a filing-agent artefact or a belt-and-braces precaution is a better explanation than a corporate event, and I searched for a take-private or merger proposal and found none. The documents are also on EDGAR full-text search and have been for nearly six months, so 'nobody wrote about it' is not the same as 'nobody could see it'. As for reaching the print: a Q2 earnings release cannot resolve a Section 16 filing-status question, and there is no call. The one live piece of corporate action here - the $10m unit repurchase programme running to 24 November 2026 - was announced 10 December 2025 and is fully public.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Georgios Prokopiou's Form 3, event date 18 March 2026, reporting 15,595,000 common units and 35,526 GP units indirectly through Dynagas Holding Ltd. at a 50.4% interest - publicly available on EDGAR since March 2026.
FY2025 annual report on the foreign-private-issuer form, restating the sponsor's control position and confirming the issuer continued on the 20-F/6-K track after the Form 3s.
Board authorised a new $10m common unit repurchase programme running through 24 November 2026, the only live corporate-action channel in the name.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No move around 18 or 30 March 2026 that the baseline captures; the only March reaction in the history block is -6.47% on 2026-03-13, which is the FY2025 results 6-K (accession 0001317861-26-000012), not the Form 3s. The Form 3s produced no volatility signature at all, which for a filing that reports no transaction is exactly what you would expect whether or not anyone noticed it. No options information exists to test a governance-event bid.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A Form 4, a 10-Q instead of a 6-K, a domestic-filer transition notice, or any 13E-3/merger filing would turn this from an artefact into a signal.

interactions: DLNG#0 and DLNG#1 both rest on live, un-archivable AIS readings taken on 2026-09-07 (Lena River at Huelva departing 25 August; Clean Energy at anchor since 5 August). I could independently confirm the Clean Energy reading by fetching the cited VesselFinder page myself, though a MarineTraffic crawl for the same IMO disagrees; I could NOT confirm the Lena River Huelva call from any source and it should be treated as single-sourced and mutable. The two findings also cut against each other on fleet exposure: #0's own verified fact - that the four 'Clean' hulls in the urgewald release belong to Dynagas Holding and Dynagas Equity Holding, not the listed partnership - establishes that only 2 of 6 listed ships carry Yamal cargo, which reduces rather than increases the partnership's sanctions concentration relative to the NGO framing, while #1 argues 2 of 6 are going to a non-producing Rio Grande. Taken together they describe a fleet with two distinct but each roughly one-third exposures, and neither finding accounts for the other's. Both also share the 29 May 2026 Q1 6-K as the document that already discloses their key premise: #0's 1 January 2027 Yamal restriction and #1's Clean Energy Q2 off-hire gap and Rio Grande delivery are both in that release. Finally, all three findings share the same channel constraint: the 8 September event is a press release plus a slide deck with no conference call, so none of them has a Q&A route into the price, and on 50,830 shares/day none can be expressed at scale by that day's close.
